method_card.title: Daily Routine and Healthy Living
method_card.content:
This lesson covers reflexive verbs for describing your daily routine and modal verbs for giving health advice in German.

GermanEnglish
sich waschento wash (oneself)
sich duschento shower
sich anziehento get dressed
sich ausziehento get undressed
sich kämmento comb one's hair
sich die Zähne putzento brush one's teeth
sich entspannento relax
aufstehen (separable)to get up
einschlafen (separable)to fall asleep
das Frühstückbreakfast
man muss + Infinitivyou must (general advice)
man soll + Infinitivyou should (general advice)
um ... zu + Infinitivin order to ...

Grammar focus — Reflexive verbs: Reflexive verbs use a reflexive pronoun that refers back to the subject. For most reflexive verbs, this pronoun is in the accusative case: Ich wasche mich. (I wash myself.) But when there is a separate direct object, the pronoun moves to the dative: Ich wasche mir die Hände. (I wash my hands — die Hände is the direct object, so mir = to myself.) The same applies to sich die Zähne putzen: Ich putze mir die Zähne.

Separable verbs split in main clauses: the prefix moves to the end. So aufstehen → Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf. In subordinate clauses, the verb stays whole at the end: weil ich um sieben Uhr aufstehe.

Modal verbs: Modal at position 2, main verb as infinitive at clause end. Man muss täglich Sport treiben. (You must do sport every day.)

Model: Ich stehe um halb sieben auf und dusche mich. Danach ziehe ich mich an und putze mir die Zähne. Man muss früh schlafen gehen, um ausgeschlafen zu sein. (I get up at half past six and shower. Afterwards I get dressed and brush my teeth. You must go to sleep early in order to be well rested.)
steps: Learn the reflexive verbs for daily routine with their correct pronouns (mich/mir)
Master separable verbs: prefix moves to the end in main clauses (aufstehen → ich stehe... auf)
Practice modal verb sentences with man muss / man soll and the infinitive at the END
Build full sentences combining time expressions, reflexive verbs and subordinate clauses with weil

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — daily routine appears across speaking, writing and listening tasks

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf und wasche mich.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Spot the separable verb: Ich stehe ... auf. The prefix auf- is at the END of the clause. The base verb is aufstehen (to get up).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: um sieben Uhr = at seven o'clock. und = and. wasche mich = wash myself (reflexive: sich waschen, accusative pronoun mich).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I get up at seven o'clock and wash myself.

worked_examples.question: Why is the pronoun 'mir' used in 'Ich putze mir die Zähne' but 'mich' in 'Ich wasche mich'?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: In Ich wasche mich, mich (accusative) is the direct object — there is nothing else being washed, so the reflexive pronoun IS the direct object.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: In Ich putze mir die Zähne, die Zähne (the teeth) is the direct object. There are now TWO objects. The reflexive pronoun moves to the dative: mir = to myself.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Rule: if there is a separate direct object after the reflexive verb, use the dative reflexive pronoun (mir, dir, sich...). If the reflexive pronoun IS the direct object, use accusative (mich, dich, sich...).

worked_examples.question: Translate into German: 'I get up at half past six in order to eat breakfast before school.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Separable verb: aufstehen → Ich stehe um halb sieben auf. Note: halb sieben = half past SIX in German (halfway to seven).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: 'In order to' = um ... zu + Infinitiv. The infinitive goes right at the end: um ... zu frühstücken or um ... Frühstück zu essen.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Check: verb at position 2 in main clause, prefix at end (auf), infinitive after zu at end of the um...zu phrase.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Ich stehe um halb sieben auf, um vor der Schule zu frühstücken.

bronze.question: Match the German reflexive verbs to the English meaning
Match the German daily routine words to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct reflexive pronoun

gaps.correct_explain: mich is the accusative reflexive pronoun for ich. Sich duschen takes the accusative because there is no separate direct object.

wrong.mir: mir is the dative reflexive pronoun. Use it only when there is a separate direct object (e.g. Ich wasche mir die Hände). Here there is none, so use mich.
wrong.sich: sich is the reflexive pronoun for er/sie/es and sie/Sie. For ich, use mich.

gaps.correct_explain: mich again — sich anziehen (to get dressed) takes the accusative reflexive pronoun when there is no separate direct object.

wrong.mir: mir would be correct for Ich ziehe mir die Jacke an (a specific item is the direct object). Without a named item, use mich.

bronze.question: Complete the modal verb sentence — infinitive goes to the END

gaps.rule: Modal verb — infinitive at clause end
gaps.correct_explain: After muss (modal at position 2), the main verb goes to the end as an infinitive: Sport treiben.

wrong.treibt: treibt is the conjugated er/sie form. After a modal verb, use the infinitive: treiben.
wrong.getrieben: getrieben is the past participle. Modal verbs take the infinitive, not the past participle.

gaps.correct_explain: bleiben is the infinitive that goes at the end of the um ... zu ... phrase: um gesund zu bleiben (in order to stay healthy).

wrong.bleibt: bleibt is conjugated. After zu in the um ... zu ... construction, you need the infinitive: bleiben.

bronze.question: What does 'Ich stehe um halb sieben auf' mean?
options: I get up at half past six
I get up at half past seven
I get up at seven o'clock
I get up at six o'clock

bronze.question: What does 'Man soll früh schlafen gehen, um ausgeschlafen zu sein' mean?
options: You should go to sleep early in order to be well rested
You must go to sleep early because you are tired
You should get up early in order to be healthy
One must fall asleep early and wake up rested

bronze.source_text: Jeden Morgen putze ich mir die Zähne und kämme mich.
model_answers: Every morning I brush my teeth and comb my hair.
hints: putze mir die Zähne = brush my teeth (dative reflexive — die Zähne is the direct object)
kämme mich = comb my hair / myself

silver.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank)
silver.english: She **gets up** at half past seven and **washes** herself.

gaps.correct_explain: steht is the er/sie/es conjugated form of the separable verb aufstehen. The prefix auf- separates and moves to the end of the clause.

wrong.aufsteht: aufsteht is incorrect — in a main clause the prefix separates from the verb. The conjugated part steht goes to position 2, and auf goes to the end.
wrong.stehe: stehe is the ich form. The subject is sie (she), so use steht.

gaps.rule: Separable verb prefix at clause end
gaps.correct_explain: The prefix auf moves to the end of the clause in a main sentence: Sie steht ... auf.

wrong.ein: ein is the prefix for einschlafen (to fall asleep), not aufstehen. The correct prefix here is auf.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Weil ich müde bin, gehe ich früh ins Bett schlafe.
silver.explanation: The sentence needs the separable verb einschlafen (to fall asleep), not just schlafe. The prefix ein- must be included. In a main clause after weil this is the verb-final subordinate clause — but the sentence structure here means the error is the missing prefix: the intended meaning needs schlafe ein or the sentence restructured.
silver.translation: Because I am tired, I go to bed early and fall asleep.

silver.question: Build the sentence in German
silver.english: Every morning I shower in order to wake up.

distractor_labels.mir: wrong case — sich duschen has no separate direct object, so use the accusative reflexive pronoun mich, not the dative mir

silver.source_text: I brush my teeth and get dressed before breakfast.
model_answers: Ich putze mir die Zähne und ziehe mich an, bevor ich frühstücke.
Vor dem Frühstück putze ich mir die Zähne und ziehe mich an.
hints: to brush teeth = sich die Zähne putzen (dative mir — die Zähne is the direct object)
to get dressed = sich anziehen (separable — prefix an goes to end)
before = bevor (subordinating conjunction — verb to end)

gold.question: Build the sentence in German
gold.english: I wash my hands in order to stay healthy.

distractor_labels.mich: wrong case — die Hände is the direct object, so the reflexive pronoun is dative: mir, not accusative mich
distractor_labels.waschen: wrong form — the conjugated verb goes at position 2: wasche (ich form). The infinitive belongs in the um...zu clause at the end.

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at the doctor's surgery in Germany. The doctor asks about your daily routine and health habits.

bullets.prompt: Say what time you get up and what you do first in the morning.
bullets.model_answer: Ich stehe um halb sieben auf. Zuerst dusche ich mich und dann putze ich mir die Zähne.
bullets.note: separable aufstehen (stehe ... auf), accusative mich for duschen, dative mir for die Zähne putzen

bullets.prompt: Say what you do to stay healthy (use man muss or man soll).
bullets.model_answer: Man muss täglich Sport treiben und man soll genug Wasser trinken, um gesund zu bleiben.
bullets.note: modal man muss + infinitive at end, man soll + infinitive, um...zu

bullets.prompt: Ask the doctor what you should do to sleep better.
bullets.model_answer: Was soll ich machen, um besser zu schlafen?
bullets.note: Sie register — addressing doctor formally; soll + infinitive at end; um...zu with besser

bullets.prompt: Say you will try to go to bed earlier from now on.
bullets.model_answer: Ab jetzt werde ich versuchen, früher ins Bett zu gehen.
bullets.note: future tense werde + versuchen; infinitive construction früher ins Bett zu gehen

gold.question: Complete the sentence — type the missing words (Higher grammar: reflexive pronoun case)
gold.english: Every evening I wash **my hands** (dative) and then I **relax** (accusative).
sentence_parts: die Hände und dann entspanne ich

gaps.rule: Dative reflexive pronoun — direct object present
gaps.correct_explain: mir is the dative reflexive pronoun. Die Hände is the direct object (accusative), so the reflexive pronoun shifts to the dative: Ich wasche mir die Hände.

wrong.mich: mich would be correct if there were no direct object (e.g. Ich wasche mich = I wash myself). But here die Hände is the direct object, so use the dative mir.

gaps.rule: Accusative reflexive pronoun — no direct object
gaps.correct_explain: mich is the accusative reflexive pronoun. Sich entspannen has no separate direct object, so the reflexive pronoun stays accusative.

wrong.mir: mir (dative) is only used when there is a separate direct object. Here there is none, so use mich.
